title.narrative: Activity under preparation Sustainable raw materials value chains between the EU and Argentina

description.narrative:
The Action aims to play a catalyst role for private sector investment into critical raw materials projects (¿EU-Argentina CRM Catalyst¿) focussing on the development of CRM projects in Argentina that are of strategic interest to the EU. The ultimate aim is to contribute to secure sustainable, resilient, and responsible supply chains that are mutually beneficial for Argentina and the EU.

This Action contributes to the 360-degree approach, improving the conditions for investment in Argentina¿s mining sector and creating opportunities for European actors across CRM value chains. It targets four key areas with strong development potential, aiming to enhance investment conditions and facilitate EU engagement throughout different segments of the value chain:

1) Enabling infrastructure - such as electric transmission lines, renewable energy, and sustainable transport modalities ¿ current lack of infrastructure hampers large-scale mining investments. Several projects of strategic interest to the EU are geographically clustered, responding to the need for joint efforts to develop infrastructure. The Action will support the preparation of coordinated, bankable investment plans - potentially through PPPs - by mobilising technical assistance, building strong business cases that can attract financing from Development Finance Institutions (DFIs) and International Finance Institutions (IFIs) under Global Gateway. Environmental, governance and human rights due diligence analysis will be enhanced, accompanying investment opportunities.

2) Skilled workforce ¿ there is currently an important gap between the availability of skilled labour in the mining provinces and the needs of the raw materials investment projects. The Action will support technical training for local population, including women and individuals from disadvantaged backgrounds, to facilitate access to decent jobs. Emphasis will be placed on aligning skills development with the concrete needs of companies and service providers involved in CRM projects of strategic interest to the EU. Embedding skills interventions in the CRM value chain is expected to unlock employment opportunities and enhance local value creation for a mutually beneficial partnership.

3) Governance of mining sector by the local authorities ¿ to contribute to enhance regulatory consistency, (including environmental and social requirements) across provinces. This Action will support improved governance by strengthening the capacities of Argentine authorities, mainly at provincial level and within interprovincial coordination bodies. The aim is to enhance coherence and institutional predictability for the investors in key areas such as environmental standards and permitting processes, promoting equality, inclusiveness and gender-sensitive approaches across the sector.

4) Research and Innovation ¿ connecting Argentina to EU research and innovation networks relevant to its mining ecosystem. The Action will organise targeted scientific diplomacy/business missions to foster engagement. These missions will facilitate direct exchanges between Argentine and European research institutions, mining companies, and policymakers, enabling the identification of joint research priorities, matchmaking for project consortia, and exploration of funding opportunities. By anchoring these missions around major mining events and including field visits, the Action will create tangible entry points for Argentine participation in EU R&I networks and enhance collaboration on science, innovation, and sustainable mining technology.
